title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash with Nokedli Dumplings
dek: Tender bone-in chicken simmers in a brick-red sweet-paprika sauce, then meets soft hand-cut egg dumplings and a cool swirl of sour cream.
image_alt: Hungarian chicken paprikash with orange-red sour-cream paprika sauce over small hand-cut egg dumplings, garnished with fresh herbs
ingredients: 3 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks, about 8 pieces
2 tsp kosher salt, divided
3/4 tsp ground black pepper, divided
2 tbsp neutral oil or chicken fat
2 medium yellow onions, finely diced, about 2 1/2 cups
1 small red bell pepper, seeded and finely diced
3 garlic cloves, finely grated
3 tbsp Hungarian sweet paprika
1/4 tsp Hungarian hot paprika or cayenne, optional
1 medium ripe tomato, seeded and grated, or 1/2 cup canned crushed tomatoes
1 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
3/4 cup full-fat sour cream, at room temperature
1 tbsp all-purpose flour, for the sauce
2 cups all-purpose flour, 240 g, for the dumplings
1 tsp kosher salt, for the dumplings
3 large eggs
2/3 cup water, plus up to 2 tbsp as needed
2 tbsp unsalted butter
2 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley, for serving

instructions.name: Season and dry the chicken
instructions.text: Pat the chicken very dry, then season it on all sides with 1 1/2 teaspoons kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Let it stand for 15 minutes while you dice the vegetables. Keep the raw-chicken tray and utensils separate from the dumpling workspace.

instructions.name: Brown the chicken in batches
instructions.text: Heat the oil in a wide 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high. Add the chicken skin-side down without crowding and brown for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once. Transfer each golden batch to a clean plate; the chicken will finish cooking in the sauce.

instructions.name: Build the paprika base
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onions, bell pepper, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and remaining 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden. Add the garlic for 30 seconds. Pull the pot off the heat, stir in both paprikas for 20 seconds, then immediately add the tomato so the spice blooms without scorching and becoming bitter.

instructions.name: Braise the chicken gently
instructions.text: Stir in the broth, scraping up the browned bits. Nestle the chicken into the sauce skin-side up and bring just to a simmer. Cover partially, reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 30 to 38 minutes, turning the pieces once, until the thickest meat away from bone reaches at least 165°F. Move the cooked chicken to a clean platter and tent loosely.

instructions.name: Mix and rest the nokedli batter
instructions.text: While the chicken braises, whisk 2 cups flour and 1 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Beat in the eggs and 2/3 cup water with a sturdy spoon just until a thick, sticky batter forms. Add the remaining water 1 tablespoon at a time only if needed; the batter should fall slowly from the spoon. Rest for 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Cut and cook the dumplings
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a steady boil. Working in three batches, spread batter on a damp cutting board and flick 1/2-inch pieces into the water with the back of a knife, or press it through a spaetzle maker. Stir once and cook for 2 minutes after the dumplings float. Lift them into a colander, drain well and toss with the butter.

instructions.name: Temper the sour cream
instructions.text: Whisk the sour cream and 1 tablespoon flour until smooth. Whisk in 1/2 cup of the hot paprika sauce a spoonful at a time, then take the pot off the heat and stir the tempered mixture into the remaining sauce. Warm over low for 2 to 3 minutes until lightly thickened; do not boil or the sour cream may split.

instructions.name: Finish and serve
instructions.text: Taste the sauce and adjust salt. Return the chicken and any platter juices to the pot for 3 minutes over low heat, keeping every piece above 165°F. Spoon buttered nokedli into warm shallow bowls, top with chicken and plenty of paprika sauce, and finish with parsley and an optional small spoonful of sour cream.

why_it_works: Removing the pot from direct heat before adding paprika protects its sweet, fruity flavor; tomato and broth then stop the spice from scorching.
Bone-in chicken develops a fuller sauce while a gentle, partially covered braise keeps the skin from turning rubbery and the meat from drying out.
Tempering room-temperature sour cream with hot sauce and avoiding a final boil produces a smooth, tangy finish instead of curds.
swaps: Use all thighs or all drumsticks if preferred, keeping the total near 3 pounds. Boneless pieces cook faster, so start checking at 18 minutes and still verify 165°F.
For store-bought noodles, replace the nokedli with 12 ounces dry wide egg noodles cooked and buttered according to the package. The result is convenient but less traditional in texture.
Full-fat plain Greek yogurt can replace sour cream. Temper it carefully off heat and do not boil; lower-fat yogurt is more likely to separate.
storage: Refrigerate chicken and sauce in one shallow airtight container and dumplings in another within 2 hours for up to 4 days. Reheat the chicken gently in a covered saucepan over medium-low, adding a splash of broth and stirring without boiling, until the thickest piece reaches 165°F. Warm dumplings separately with a teaspoon of water and a little butter. Freeze the chicken and paprika sauce for up to 2 months, but make fresh dumplings after thawing for the best texture.
notes: The 105-minute total includes the 15-minute chicken seasoning and dumpling-batter rest, which overlap with vegetable prep and braising.
Paprika is the defining ingredient, so use a fresh Hungarian sweet paprika rather than smoked paprika; old spice gives color but very little aroma.

The licensed photograph visibly shows one sauced chicken portion centered over small irregular egg dumplings with a creamy paprika coating and herb garnish; the recipe matches that finished form, sauce and presentation.

faqs.q: Why did my chicken paprikash sauce taste bitter?
faqs.a: Paprika scorches quickly in a hot, dry pot. Move the pot off heat before stirring it into the softened onions, work for only about 20 seconds, and add tomato promptly to cool the mixture.

faqs.q: Can I make nokedli without a spaetzle maker?
faqs.a: Yes. Put one-third of the sticky batter on a damp cutting board held over the pot and use the back of a wet knife to flick narrow 1/2-inch pieces into the water. Small irregular shapes are correct and cook evenly.

faqs.q: How do I keep sour cream from curdling in paprikash?
faqs.a: Use full-fat sour cream at room temperature, whisk it smooth with flour, gradually warm it with hot sauce, and stir it into the pot off heat. Reheat only gently and never let the finished sauce boil.

title: Sicilian Pasta alla Norma with Roasted Eggplant & Ricotta Salata
dek: Rigatoni, concentrated tomato sauce and caramelized eggplant come together with basil and salty ricotta salata for a satisfying meatless pasta.
image_alt: Rigatoni in chunky tomato sauce with browned eggplant slices, grated ricotta salata and fresh basil on a blue plate
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb globe eggplant, about 1 large, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch half-moons
1 1/4 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more for the pasta water
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
4 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
1 can whole peeled tomatoes, 28 oz, crushed by hand with their juices
1/4 tsp granulated sugar, only if the tomatoes taste sharp
12 oz rigatoni or mezze rigatoni
3/4 cup loosely packed fresh basil leaves, divided
3 oz ricotta salata, finely grated, about 3/4 cup, divided
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

instructions.name: Heat the oven and season the eggplant
instructions.text: Arrange racks in the upper and lower thirds and heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the eggplant half-moons with 3/4 teaspoon salt and let them stand for 10 minutes. Blot away the beads of moisture, then toss with 2 1/2 tablespoons olive oil and black pepper.

instructions.name: Roast until deeply browned
instructions.text: Spread the eggplant in one layer across two rimmed sheet pans so the pieces do not overlap. Roast for 24 to 28 minutes, switching the pans and turning the slices halfway, until the centers are creamy and the edges are browned. Reserve six attractive slices for the top and roughly chop the rest.

instructions.name: Build the tomato-basil sauce
instructions.text: While the eggplant roasts, warm 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-low. Add the garlic and pepper flakes; cook for 45 seconds without browning. Add the crushed tomatoes, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and sugar only if needed. Simmer uncovered for 18 to 22 minutes until glossy and thick enough to leave a brief trail when stirred. Tear in half the basil.

instructions.name: Boil the rigatoni
instructions.text: Bring 4 quarts water to a boil and season it until pleasantly salty. Add the rigatoni and cook 2 minutes shy of the package's al dente time. Before draining, scoop out 1 cup pasta water. Drain thoroughly but do not rinse.

instructions.name: Finish the pasta in the sauce
instructions.text: Add the hot rigatoni and chopped roasted eggplant to the skillet. Toss over medium heat for 2 minutes, adding reserved pasta water 2 tablespoons at a time until the sauce clings inside and outside every tube. Fold in half the ricotta salata and most of the remaining basil.

instructions.name: Plate with visible eggplant
instructions.text: Divide the pasta among four warm plates. Arrange the reserved browned eggplant slices around and over the rigatoni, matching the dish's characteristic presentation. Finish with the remaining ricotta salata and basil, then serve immediately.

why_it_works: A brief salting and thorough blot remove surface moisture, while two uncrowded hot pans roast the eggplant instead of steaming it.
Finishing undercooked rigatoni in concentrated tomato sauce lets starch bind the sauce to the pasta, and reserved cooking water controls the final gloss.
Adding ricotta salata in two stages seasons the sauce from within while preserving a fresh salty finish that contrasts with sweet tomato and eggplant.
swaps: Use ziti, penne rigate or another sturdy tube pasta in place of rigatoni. Keep the dry weight at 12 ounces and reserve pasta water before draining.
If ricotta salata is unavailable, use a mix of 2 ounces finely grated pecorino Romano and 1 ounce crumbled feta. It is not identical, so salt the sauce conservatively.
Fresh plum tomatoes can replace canned in peak season. Peel and crush 2 pounds, then simmer 5 to 10 minutes longer to reach the same concentrated texture.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours for up to 4 days. Reheat a portion in a covered skillet over medium-low with 1 to 2 tablespoons water until steaming and 165°F, then uncover briefly to restore the sauce's cling. Freeze the tomato-eggplant sauce without pasta for up to 2 months; cooked rigatoni becomes soft after freezing.
notes: Choose a firm, glossy eggplant that feels heavy for its size. Very large seedy specimens can taste bitter and absorb more oil.
Ricotta salata is a firm, aged salted cheese, not the soft tub ricotta used for lasagna. Grate it finely so a modest amount seasons the entire dish.

The licensed photograph clearly shows ridged tube pasta in tomato sauce with broad browned eggplant slices, grated white cheese and basil; the recipe preserves those visible ingredients and plated arrangement.

faqs.q: Why is my roasted eggplant rubbery instead of creamy?
faqs.a: The slices were probably crowded, cut too thick or removed before their centers softened. Use two pans, leave space around every 1/2-inch slice and roast until both faces brown and the centers yield easily to a fork.

faqs.q: Do I have to peel eggplant for Pasta alla Norma?
faqs.a: No. The skin gives the half-moons structure and a dark border that remains visible on the plate. Peel alternating strips only if the eggplant has unusually tough skin.

faqs.q: Can I prepare the sauce ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Roast the eggplant and cook the tomato sauce up to 2 days ahead, refrigerating them separately. Rewarm both while the pasta boils, then combine with fresh basil, cheese and pasta water for the best texture.

title: Honey-Pistachio Baklava with Orange-Blossom Syrup
dek: Dozens of crisp buttered phyllo layers surround a generous pistachio filling, while a bright honey and orange-blossom syrup keeps every diamond fragrant and tender-crisp.
image_alt: Close-up of a square pistachio baklava showing many crisp golden phyllo layers and a thick filling of chopped green pistachios
ingredients: 1 cup granulated sugar, 200 g
3/4 cup water
1/2 cup mild honey, 170 g
2 wide strips lemon peel, yellow part only
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
1 tbsp orange-blossom water
3 1/2 cups shelled unsalted pistachios, 450 g, divided
2 tbsp granulated sugar
1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
1/4 tsp fine sea salt
1 package frozen phyllo dough, 16 oz, thawed overnight in the refrigerator
1 1/4 cups unsalted butter, 285 g, melted and kept warm

instructions.name: Cook and cool the syrup
instructions.text: Combine 1 cup sugar, water, honey and lemon peel in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring only until the sugar dissolves. Simmer without stirring for 6 minutes. Remove from heat, stir in lemon juice and orange-blossom water, discard the peel and cool completely. Keep the hot syrup away from children and turn the saucepan handle inward.

instructions.name: Prepare the pan and pistachios
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Brush a 9-by-13-inch glass baking dish with melted butter. Pulse 3 cups pistachios, 2 tablespoons sugar, cinnamon and salt in a food processor in short bursts until mostly coarse crumbs with some pea-size pieces; do not grind them into paste. Finely chop the remaining 1/2 cup pistachios for garnish.

instructions.name: Size and protect the phyllo
instructions.text: Unroll the phyllo and trim the stack to fit the baking dish. Cover it immediately with plastic wrap and then a barely damp kitchen towel. Keep the sheets covered whenever you are not lifting one; exposed phyllo dries and cracks within minutes.

instructions.name: Build the lower crisp layers
instructions.text: Lay one phyllo sheet in the buttered dish and brush it lightly from edge to edge with warm butter. Repeat until 10 sheets are stacked. Scatter one-third of the coarse pistachio mixture evenly over the surface without pressing it down.

instructions.name: Layer the filling and top
instructions.text: Add 5 more buttered phyllo sheets, then another third of the pistachio mixture. Repeat with 5 buttered sheets and the final third of filling. Finish with 10 buttered sheets, brushing the top generously. If your package has fewer than 30 usable sheets, keep the bottom and top stacks even and divide the remainder between the middle layers.

instructions.name: Cut before baking
instructions.text: With a very sharp knife, cut through every layer into four long strips, then make diagonal cuts about 1 1/2 inches apart to form 24 diamonds. Hold the top gently with your free hand so the phyllo does not lift. Spoon any remaining butter along the cut lines.

instructions.name: Bake until deeply golden
instructions.text: Bake for 45 to 52 minutes, rotating the dish after 30 minutes, until the top and cut edges are evenly deep gold and crisp. Pale phyllo will soften quickly under syrup, so use color rather than only the clock as the doneness cue.

instructions.name: Syrup and rest
instructions.text: Set the hot baking dish on a heatproof rack. Slowly ladle the completely cooled syrup over the hot baklava, concentrating along the cut lines; it will sizzle. Scatter the finely chopped pistachios over the center of each diamond. Cool uncovered for at least 3 hours so the syrup settles and the upper layers stay crisp before recutting and serving.

why_it_works: Cool syrup meeting hot pastry absorbs gradually without steaming every upper layer, preserving the contrast between crisp phyllo and juicy nut filling.
Coarse rather than powdered pistachios create the visible textured center and leave air channels for syrup between the pastry layers.
Cutting all the way through before baking prevents the fragile golden top from shattering later and channels butter and syrup into every portion.
swaps: Replace up to half the pistachios with walnuts for a deeper, less costly filling. Keep the total nut weight at 450 grams and chop to the same coarse texture.
If orange-blossom water is unavailable, use 1 teaspoon finely grated orange zest in the syrup. The aroma is different but still bright; do not substitute orange extract at the same volume.
A light-colored metal 9-by-13-inch pan can replace glass. Begin checking at 42 minutes because metal browns the bottom faster, and pour the syrup carefully because the pan will be very hot.
storage: Keep completely cooled baklava loosely covered at cool room temperature for up to 5 days; an airtight container softens the top. For longer storage, freeze the cut pieces in a rigid airtight container with parchment between layers for up to 2 months. Thaw uncovered at room temperature for 1 hour. Refrigeration is safe but makes the honey-butter filling firm and the phyllo less crisp.
notes: The 265-minute total includes a 3-hour uncovered rest after syruping; the pastry is baked in 50 minutes but slices cleanly and tastes more balanced after standing.
Thaw phyllo overnight in its unopened package, then let it sit at room temperature for 1 hour before unrolling. Condensation on cold sheets makes them stick together.

The licensed photograph provides a clear cross-section of deeply layered golden phyllo and a substantial chopped-pistachio center; the recipe matches those visible proportions, texture and square serving form.

faqs.q: Why did my baklava turn soggy?
faqs.a: The pastry may have been underbaked, the syrup and pastry were both hot, or the finished pan was covered while warm. Bake to deep gold, use fully cooled syrup on hot pastry and cool uncovered for at least 3 hours.

faqs.q: How do I keep phyllo from tearing while I work?
faqs.a: Thaw it slowly in the sealed package, bring it to room temperature before opening and keep the stack under plastic plus a barely damp towel. Small tears are harmless because the sheets overlap; patch them with another buttered piece.

faqs.q: Can I assemble pistachio baklava ahead and bake later?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemble and cut it up to 1 day ahead, cover the pan tightly and refrigerate. Let it stand at room temperature while the oven heats, then bake as directed and use syrup made and chilled separately.
